scope: Offline structural inspection of Iggy payloads embedded in cooked IggyPlayer exports; no game launch or asset replacement

inspector.output_policy: Parses bounded type-0 index streams, maps every object start to a candidate layout, verifies physical ordering/non-overlap, summarizes stream boundaries and relative fields, records kind-3 dual-pointer candidate spans and their boundary markers, profiles kind-1 record-end regions and kind-4 compressed/image envelopes, and validates kind-6 string pointers without retaining source text or payload bytes. A separate bounded side-block scan records only signed-i32 candidate references that resolve to aligned object starts.
limitations: Object kinds 1, 3, and 4 remain semantically unnamed; candidate field layouts and target locations do not decode their structures or references.
No display-list, MovieClip, button, event, script, focus, or navigation graph has been reconstructed.
The semantic meaning of type-0 stream partitions and opaque metadata type codes is not yet known.
Successful payload extraction and structural parsing do not prove that the game loads a modified loose asset.

Kind-1 candidate regions are bounded from field 0x48 target to the next object pointer; their ownership and internal structure are not established, and opaque-region classification is not semantic decoding.

Kind-3 fields 0x38/0x40 delimit candidate byte spans in most objects and field 0x40 targets a repeated two-u64 marker; this is a structural relationship only, not a decoded array/schema or proven display reference.
Signed-i32 values in kind-1/kind-3 side blocks that land on object starts are candidate links only; they do not prove parent-child, shape, bitmap, or script semantics.
inspector.layout_interpretation: A command beginning exactly at an object pointer start selects an index-table entry whose declared size and local-offset/type-code metadata form a candidate record layout. These layouts are proven consistent per kind in the three fixed-build movies; kinds 1, 3, and 4 remain semantically unnamed.
inspector.relative_field_method: For each index metadata type-code-2 field, classify field_offset + u64_value against the candidate record end, next object start, and movie bounds. Kind-6 field 0x60 is separately verified by decoding its target as bounded UTF-16. Kind-3 field 0x40 records only the first two u64 values and distance to the next object start; kind-4 field 0x48 recognizes bounded complete zlib streams or length-prefixed JPEG data. These are byte-level payload observations, not semantic names or proof of display-reference meaning.
inspector.index_stream_interpretation: In the three fixed-build movies, matched object starts are disjoint and monotonically ordered by type-0 subfile; settings/character streams reuse the same table definition within each movie. The next stream first command begins at the previous stream final offset for settings and 4 bytes later for character. This establishes address ordering and boundary relationships, not the intended runtime meaning of the stream split.

iggy_text_edit_experiment.status: offline same-size text replacement reparsed by the independent structural parser; does not create or alter display objects and does not prove that the game loads the modified resource

index_read_write_findings.reader_parse_entries: IggyFile.parseEntries() locates the type-1 movie; its IggyIndexParser.parseIndex call for type-0 entries is commented out.
index_read_write_findings.writer_update_flash_entry: IggyFile.updateFlashEntry() serializes a replacement movie with IggyIndexBuilder, removes all original type-0 entries, then appends one newly generated type-0 entry.
index_read_write_findings.builder_semantics: Index commands encode lengths, padding and typed arrays while advancing a cumulative serialized write position.

jpexs_26_3_0_source_check.conclusion: JPEXS 26.3.0 is not a complete editor/rebuilder for the Iggy display data used by these target assets; its general 64-bit Iggy support is insufficient for adding controls to this movie.

index_metadata_findings.parser_reads_index_metadata_as: local-offset/type-code byte pairs attached to each table entry

next_static_research: Trace the pinned Iggy DLL's parser/object-construction paths that consume kind-1/kind-3 side blocks; determine whether the 8-byte-aligned signed-i32 candidates are runtime relocations or resource references, and do not call them display-tree edges without that evidence.

Decode kind-3 candidate spans and their repeated end marker into field-level records, comparing same-length patterns across settings, character, and pause movies; preserve unnamed status until independent evidence confirms a schema.
Decode kind-1 auxiliary regions and connect validated object references to type-3/type-4/type-6 records; distinguish resource dependency links from display parent-child relationships.
Determine the binary meaning of the two type-0 index-stream partitions and relate non-object boundaries to object record regions; object starts are already mapped one-to-one.
Build a no-op read/write fixture and require byte-equivalent preservation of all unedited objects before attempting a single controlled structural edit.

Continue tracing cooked-resource override resolution and UIManagerComponent class validation; do not claim a loadable Mod page until an offline package and supported runtime path are both demonstrated.
